payload.title: Short Wedding Vows Examples Under One Minute
protect_keywords: how long should wedding vows be
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s planning a destination wedding with a generous budget, who want to say something personal at the ceremony without a long speech, and need ready-to-adapt short examples, a simple template, a clear sense of how long to speak and what words the law requires them to say.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about planning a destination wedding (single primary CTA, placed after the destination ceremony note); /magazine as a soft secondary link in the close.
payload.angle: Most short-vow lists are pasted quotes with no guidance. This one gives about 20 original vows, each timed to under a minute and grouped by tone and occasion, a fill-in-the-blanks one-minute template, our advice to keep vows to 1 to 2 minutes and time them aloud, and a plain explanation of the words Australian law requires alongside personal vows, plus what changes when you marry legally overseas.
must_include: Intro, then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways
How long vows should be: keep them to 1 to 2 minutes as our advice (not attributed); read aloud and time it

What the law requires in Australia: the celebrant's words and the vows each partner must say under the Marriage Act 1961 s45, from official sources (legislation.gov.au, Attorney-General's Department) linked inline at each claim; personal vows can sit alongside them only as the official source states; for destination couples, the legal wording follows the country where you marry legally, so ask your celebrant or registrar
About 20 original short vow examples, each under one minute, grouped: classic and timeless; romantic; modern and simple; light and funny; for him; for her; for a destination ceremony; renewal
Delivery tips: cards or memory; confirm the order on the day with your celebrant; a microphone outdoors framed as a question to ask
avoid: Lyrics, film lines, poems, quotations or competitor example vows; every example is our original writing
Any same-sex legal position (examples may be written inclusively without legal claims)
Legal wording paraphrased without an official source linked inline at the claim
Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; never implying the Advisor writes vows or handles legal paperwork
Attributing the 1 to 2 minute advice to any search engine or outside source
Research talk in the copy (sources, method, what we could or couldn't find)
Title or meta title as a question, with colons or dashes, or over 60 characters
payload.regional_scope_reason: Vow examples are not country specific; the legal section is Australian and the destination note covers other countries. Australian English and AUD-based CTA keep the AU reader. SEO to test au_focus.
payload.cannibalisation_check: No existing page targets 'short wedding vows'. /how-to-write-wedding-vows targets the writing process (this post links to it prominently and stays example-led); /expert-advice/traditional-wedding-vows and /featured/what-are-the-traditional-wedding-vows cover traditional wording (linked, not repeated); /expert-advice/vow-renewal-ideas covers renewals broadly (renewal group stays to short examples). SEO to confirm the two traditional-vows pages do not split intent with each other.
